text:
alex: Quick design question — we need an approach for region-aware routing that also supports model-variant fallback when a region is overloaded. Thinking about latency-based region selection + tier-based affinity. Thoughts?

maria: yes. two parts: 1) routing (latency + capacity) 2) fallback (model variants / quantization).

sam: For latency we currently have passive p95/p99 from traces. Should we do active probes per region per model?

jin: active probes help for cold spots. probed RTT + recent p99 gives better decision surface. but watch probe cost at scale.

riley: Tier rules: enterprise customers get region affinity (pin to customer-preferred region) + SLA fallback to warm standby region. free/dev tier: auto route to cheapest/least-loaded region, can fallback to quantized variants.

alex: Example policy sketch I'm thinking of:
```yaml
routing_policies:
  - match: {customer_tier: enterprise}
    primary: preferred_region
    fallbacks: [preferred_region_standby, nearest_region]
    latency_threshold_ms: 120
  - match: {customer_tier: dev}
    primary: cheapest_region
    fallbacks: [nearest_region, quantized_variant]
    latency_threshold_ms: 250
```

maria: Love that. A few open questions: how do we detect "overloaded" vs transient spike? and should fallback prefer same model family or cheaper variant?

sam: Overload detection: sliding window of enqueue time + tail latency + GPU utilization on region. If queue depth > X or backend util > 85% for 30s, mark degraded. fallback triggers only after short cool-down to avoid flapping.

jin: Prefer same model family with smaller context/quantized weights as first fallback. Only change family (e.g., llama2->gpt-compat) for severe outages. Need to surface quality drop in telemetry.

riley: Console UX: show route decision per request (region chosen, fallback reason, model variant) on trace flyouts. Also add a rollout control: canary fallback percentage per customer so we can test fallback quality.

alex: Telemetry requirements: per-route p50/p95/p99, fallback count, fallback latency delta, quality deltas (BLEU/embedding-sim) by prompt set, and per-customer region affinity violations.

maria: Quotas: per-region request quotas to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts. If quota exceeded, route to fallback region and increment quota_violation metric. Request throttling response should include headers: `X-Redwood-Region`, `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason`, `X-Redwood-Fallback-Model` so apps can adapt.

sam: Implementation idea: lightweight routing service in control plane with local cache on edge nodes. Decision = combine (latency_score, capacity_score, tier_weight, affinity_score). Score formula tunable via console. Keep last-good-region cache per customer to reduce churn.

jin: Important: fallbacks must be transparent in logs and allow automatic rollback of fallback rollout if quality regression exceeds threshold. Add an eval hook that runs daily on sampled requests to compare variants.

riley: UX addition: on rollout page let SRE/product pick a fallback policy template: "latency-first", "cost-first", "affinity-first". Templates prefilled with thresholds + cool-downs.

alex: Security/Privacy note: enterprise pinning must respect customer VPC/data residency. If fallback attempts to route out-of-region, require explicit customer opt-in.

ops-bot: deploy notice: routing-proto branch deployed to staging at 1764123500. Canary 5% running.

maria: Next steps: draft RFC with policy grammar, telemetry schema, and console UX mockups. I'll start the RFC and assign owners for probes, routing service, and eval hooks.

alex: Awesome — assign me and @riley for console + rollout UX. Sam/Jin take routing infra and fallback evals. We'll sync Friday 10am. :thumbsup:
